prov.onchainHint: Recorded by the Qupon program on Solana. The link opens the transaction in the explorer.
prov.verifiedHint: Re-checked against devnet: amounts, holders and the snapshot hash match the chain.
prov.simulatedHint: Not a real integration. Shown so the flow is complete; nothing leaves the demo.
prov.demoHint: Time runs fast on this series: a whole bond life takes minutes. Same maths, labelled DEMO.

actor.label: Who can do it
actor.anyoneHint: Permissionless: any wallet can push this step and the program checks every rule.

now.label: Now
now.anyone: Anyone can push this step: the program checks every rule.
now.defaulted: In default: the issuer cures it by funding the escrow; the record-date holders keep their claim.
now.trades: {ticker}: settle or cancel the open trades before the record date
now.notApproved: {ticker}: the meeting did not approve the change
now.investorVote: {ticker} bondholder meeting: holders vote until the deadline
now.investorRecord: {ticker} coupon: whoever holds the bond on the record date is paid

money.title: Where the money goes
money.stepTax: Withheld tax goes to the tax vault
money.stepAgent: Sent to the paying agent for {who}

recordDate.def: The moment that decides who gets paid: whoever holds the bond then receives the coupon, even if they sell it afterwards.

exDate.def: The first day a bond trades without the right to the next coupon. On Qupon the record date does this job: buy after it and the seller keeps the payout.

coupon.def: The interest payment a bond pays on its schedule — for these bonds, 10% a year in two halves of 50.00 ₸ per 1,000 ₸ bond.

accrued.def: The part of the next coupon earned since the last payment date. A buyer pays it to the seller on top of the clean price.

cleanDirty.def: Clean price is quoted without accrued interest; dirty price is what actually changes hands: clean plus accrued.

ytm.def: The annual return if you buy at today's price and hold to maturity, with every coupon paid on time.

entitlement.def: What one holder is owed for one action: units × amount per bond, gross, tax and net, rounded half-up per holder.

snapshot.def: An on-chain copy of every holder's balance at the record date. The sum must equal the bonds outstanding, or the action cannot continue.

snapshotHash.def: One fingerprint of the whole register: the XOR of a hash per holder. Batch order does not change it, so anyone can verify the snapshot is complete.

escrow.def: A program-owned account the issuer funds before payment. Money can only leave it to the holders, the tax vault or the paying agent recorded on-chain.

taxVault.def: Where withholding tax goes at source, per the holder's investor class, before the net amount is paid.

payoutRoute.def: Where a holder's money goes: straight to their wallet, or through the paying agent to a bank account. Only the holder's own signature can set or change it.

payingAgent.def: The bank that receives payouts for holders who chose a bank route and confirms the transfer with a reference. Bank transfer is simulated.

redemption.def: The issuer pays back the face value at maturity and the bonds are burned. On Qupon pay and burn happen in one instruction.

earlyCall.def: The issuer's right to pay back the bonds before maturity, announced as a corporate action with its own record date.

partialCall.def: An early redemption of only part of the issue. Every holder is reduced pro rata, so nobody is picked by hand.

meeting.def: A vote of holders on a change — for example a new coupon rate. One vote per snapshotted bond; the record date fixes who can vote.

quorum.def: The minimum share of the snapshotted bonds that must vote for a meeting to count. Each series sets it in its terms.

registrar.def: The operator that keeps the register: announces actions from the KASE notice, checks the snapshot reconciles, and reports back.

permissionless.def: Any wallet can push this step forward. The program checks every rule, so nobody — not even the issuer — can stall a funded payment.

transferHook.def: A check the bond token runs on every transfer. After the record date a position moves only once it is snapshotted, so trading never stops.

tokenPause.def: The legacy way to freeze a mint for a record date: transfers are paused until the snapshot is final. New hooked series use the transfer hook instead.

dvp.def: A secondary trade where bonds and cash swap in one settlement: the seller's bonds sit in escrow until the buyer's cash arrives.

default.def: The payment date plus one grace day passed and the escrow is short. Anyone can record it on-chain; the debt stays public until cured.

graceDay.def: The one series day after a payment date during which the issuer may still fund the escrow. Once it passes with the escrow short, anyone can record the default.

cure.def: Late funding of a defaulted payment. Holders on the record date are still the ones paid.

sas.def: A KYC proof from the Solana Attestation Service bound to the wallet. Only attested investors can hold bonds or get paid.

demoClock.def: A series option that maps one bond day to a few seconds, so a whole life — coupons, default, redemption — plays out in minutes. Refused on mainnet.

dayCount.def: Day-count convention: every month counts as 30 days and a year as 360, as in KASE coupon schedules.

noticeAnchor.def: The sha256 hash of a seev.031 notice, written on-chain once. Any copy of the file can be checked against it forever.

seev031.def: ISO 20022 corporate-action notification: the announcement custodians and banks read.

seev036.def: ISO 20022 movement confirmation: one per holder, stating what was paid and when.
